newsitem.title: USA: U.S. black group begins pre-election convention.
newsitem.headline: U.S. black group begins pre-election convention.

text.p: Organisers of the Million Man March, last year's peaceful gathering of hundreds of thousands of black men in Washington, began a three-day convention Friday to educate and mobilise black voters for the coming U.S. election.
Up to 30,000 people were expected to attend events over the weekend in the St. Louis area, and vote on a national agenda tailored to black American concerns.

The agenda would spur blacks to "mobilize our constitutencies ... for political empowerment," said Benjamin Chavis, head of this weekend's National African-American Summit and an organiser, along with Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, of the Oct. 16, 1995, Million Man March.
Farrakhan will speak Saturday in St. Louis' football stadium, the Trans World Dome, to what was expected to be the largest gathering of the three-day meeting.

One subject Chavis said would be addressed during the convention was the U.S. government's recent decision to bar Farrakhan from accepting a $1 billion gift from Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, citing Libya's alleged support of terrorism. Farrakhan said the money would have been used to help poor American blacks.
After the Million Man March, many questioned whether the event's messages of raising black men's sense of responsiblity to their families and communities would produce any follow-up action.
Activists have registered 1 million mostly black new voters since the march, Chavis said, adding that the causes had been carried on by several smaller groups, many associated with churches.
"The black vote is not for sale. The black vote cannot be manipulated," Chavis said, adding that no political candidates from any party would be endorsed.
